conceptTag: Choose which value to lead with
readerTitle: Six good reasons to hire you, and no one calls
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (홈 수리 서비스 → 임대인 → 대기업 이전 지원팀) · 모든 인물과 상황은 설명용
insight: 무엇을 앞세울지는 내 강점 목록이 아니라, 지금 읽는 고객의 가장 큰 고통과 그 고객의 대안이 정한다.
misconception: 장점을 많이 나열할수록 더 설득력 있다. 가장 좋은 강점 하나를 모든 고객에게 똑같이 앞세우면 된다.

sources.text: 이 유닛의 개념 레슨 (진통제 vs 비타민, 고객의 차선책, 고객 쪽 전환 비용)을 시뮬레이션으로 적용
모든 인물, 수치, 상황은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 사례는 가상입니다. 통계나 실제 기업 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다. '5 working days', '15%', '5 trial moves'는 설명용 가정입니다.
'고객 10명에게 물었다'는 장면은 가상이며 연구 결과처럼 읽히지 않도록 문장을 확인하세요.
6번 카드의 '깨진 약속이 약속이 없는 것보다 더 해롭다'는 일반적 서술입니다. 특정 연구 인용으로 바꾸지 마세요.

cards.title: Six good reasons to hire you, and no one calls
body: Rosa runs a four-person home repair business. Her crews are insured, fairly priced, tidy, quick and local, and they send photos when a job is done.
Her flyer lists all six. Calls are flat. Over the next three cards, you make Rosa's calls.

image.label: A crowded flyer with six equal-sized claims
image.brief: 현관 문에 붙은 홈 수리 전단지. 'Insured', 'Fair prices', 'Tidy', 'Quick', 'Local', 'Photo reports' 여섯 문구가 모두 같은 크기라 눈에 띄는 것이 없음. 옆에 조용한 전화기. 실제 브랜드나 로고 없음.

cards.title: One big line on the flyer
body: Rosa asks ten recent customers why they called her. Most tell the same story: the last handyman never showed up, or came days late.
She has room for one big line. What should it say?

options.feedback: Customers start comparing quotes line by line, and Rosa wins only when she's cheapest. Price wasn't what hurt them.

options.text: On time, or your first hour is free
options.feedback: Callers repeat the promise back on the phone. It names the pain they already felt, and the guarantee makes it believable.
Warm and true, and it offers some emotional value. But every rival's van says the same, so it doesn't explain why Rosa.

cards.title: A new kind of customer: landlords
body: Say you chose the on-time promise. Calls pick up, and some landlords ask about fixing flats between tenants. Most already use a regular contractor who turns up eventually.
Every empty week is a week without rent. What should Rosa lead with for landlords?

options.feedback: It still matters, but their current contractor shows up too. It doesn't beat what landlords already do.

options.text: Flat ready for the next tenant in five working days, with a photo report so you never need to visit
options.feedback: It targets their costliest problem, empty weeks, and the photos save trips. Their regular contractor doesn't offer that.

options.text: Lower rates than your current contractor
options.feedback: A few landlords try her once. But a small saving rarely outweighs a week of lost rent, so she gets picked on price and dropped on price.

cards.title: A team inside a big company
body: Say you chose the five-day turnaround. Word spreads, and the relocation team at a large local employer calls. They set up flats for new hires. Their manager is judged on new hires starting their first week without problems.
They already have a vendor. Changing means paperwork, a new contact and the risk of a bad first week. How should Rosa open?

options.text: Send the full list of services and a price sheet
options.feedback: Back to the six-item flyer. The manager has to work out why it matters, and the easy answer is to stay put.

options.text: Offer to take the next five moves: one named contact, a photo check the day before each arrival, no long contract
options.feedback: It leads with what the manager is judged on and makes trying Rosa cheap. The small trial lowers the cost of switching.

options.text: Promise to beat the current vendor's price by 15%
options.feedback: Finance may like it, but the manager's worry isn't budget. Saving money on a move that goes wrong is a bad trade for them.

cards.title: Same crew, three different first lines.
body: Rosa's crew didn't change. What she put first did, because each reader had a different pain and a different alternative.

breakdown.label: Homeowners
breakdown.detail: Pain: handymen who don't show up

breakdown.label: Relocation team
breakdown.detail: Pain: a new hire's bad first week

cards.softwareNote: A software product does the same with landing pages: one for the user who wants less busywork, another for the manager who signs off and worries about risk.

cards.title: Your lead value
body: Your **lead value** is the one benefit you put first. It isn't your best feature. It's the benefit that answers this customer's sharpest pain *and* beats what they'd do without you.
Rosa's other strengths didn't disappear. They became supporting reasons, there to back up the headline once it caught attention.

image.label: One large headline above smaller supporting reasons
image.brief: 같은 전단지의 '전'과 '후' 비교. 왼쪽은 여섯 문구가 같은 크기, 오른쪽은 'On time, or your first hour is free'가 크게 위에 있고 나머지 다섯 개가 작게 아래에 정리됨. 로고 없음.

cards.title: A lead line is a promise, and promises cost.
body: Rosa's free hour only works if her crews really are on time. A lead you can't deliver hurts more than no lead at all.
And customers' answers are only a start. Watch what they do: which line brings calls, which offer gets signed. Change the lead when behavior says so.

cards.title: Lead with their pain, not your list.
body: Each decision used an idea from this unit:
list: Decision 1, *painkillers vs vitamins:* lead with the pain customers already feel
Decision 2, *next best alternative:* lead where you beat what they do now
Decision 3, *switching costs:* make it cheap and safe to try you
cards.callout: **Try it today:** ask three recent customers why they picked you over what they did before. Is that reason the first line people see?
